conventions.shape: tlgr [global flags] <noun> [<sub-noun>] <verb> [<target>] [<args>] [--flags]; paths are at most 3 levels.

refs.chat: @username | peer id (-100… for channels/supergroups) | t.me/… | tg://… | me | saved
refs.msg_id: message id inside <chat>; a t.me message link is accepted wherever a <chat> <msg_id> pair is expected
refs.topic: --topic <id> on any message command; `chat topic *` manages them
refs.variadic: multiple ids are variadic positionals (message delete <chat> <id>...)

conventions.durations: 30s | 5m | 2h | 7d | forever; timestamps are ISO-8601 in, RFC-3339 UTC out

short_flags.-n: bound to --limit on list/search ops only; --dry-run has no short form (STYLE listed -n for both)

verbs.rule: a verb outside the STYLE list is only allowed when it names a Telegram/daemon operation with no synonym in the list; noun tails were renamed to <sub-noun> <verb>.

additions.giveaway: giveaways and gift codes are a first-class GUI surface, distinct from `gift`
additions.sync: update-state / getDifference plumbing, distinct from the `catchup` unread digest
additions.net: network + data-centre diagnostics (ping, dc, usage), distinct from `proxy`
additions.webhook: outbound event delivery configuration, sibling of `events`/`watch`
additions.passport: Telegram Passport is its own GUI surface
additions.completion: v1 path (`tlgr completion bash|zsh|fish`) kept for compatibility
additions.status: v1 shortcut; a single top-level command, not a noun with verbs
additions.watch: v1 shortcut; a single top-level command
additions.schema: v1 shortcut; a single top-level command

cross_cutting.redact: --redact (and `[defaults] redact = true`) never prints access hashes, file references, invite hashes or session tokens; they are replaced by `"<redacted>"`. Access hashes are never printed by default in any human output and only under `--json --no-redact`.
cross_cutting.media_upload_mirror: `media upload` and `message send --file` share one contract: the same file flags, the same SendOptions, the same MediaInfo output.
cross_cutting.reply_markup: `--reply-markup JSON` uses the schema defined by the bots/payments group; `message get --json` renders the same schema in `reply_markup`, so a button read back can be pressed with `bot press`.
cross_cutting.sticker_split: `sticker set *` = installed sticker/emoji sets (server state); `sticker pack *` = authoring a set you own; `emoji set *` are aliases of `sticker set *`.
cross_cutting.catchup_vs_sync: `chat catchup` (v1) is the unread digest; `sync catch-up` is updates.getDifference plumbing.
cross_cutting.takeout: takeout lives under the `export` noun (account group). `daemon takeout *` are aliases.
cross_cutting.rights_vocabulary: admin/banned rights keywords come from the groups_channels_admin group and are used verbatim by `chat admin promote`, `chat permission set`, `chat member restrict` and `bot default-rights set`.
cross_cutting.privacy_keys: privacy keys/rules come from account_security_privacy and are used by `privacy set`, `privacy global set`, `story blocklist set` and `contact close-friends set`.
cross_cutting.event_types: event type names come from updates_network_daemon (`events list`) and are the only values accepted by `watch --events`, `job add --on` and `webhook set --events`.

impl.notes: The honest-limits surface an agent should read before planning. Fixed entries: secret chats are envelope-only (Telethon has no MTProto 2.0 e2e layer); PFS/temporary auth keys are not implemented (auth.bindTempAuthKey), so protecting the session file is the mitigation; call media needs tgcalls and is out of scope; push registration is out of scope (the daemon holds a socket). Policy entries: tlgr never fakes a read receipt — not calling messages.readHistory is allowed, but a switch that reads and hides the receipt would violate api terms 1.4; tlgr never suppresses typing status; tlgr never misrepresents online status (see presence.mode, default 'off' = announce nothing); tlgr never attempts a Play Integrity / APNs / reCAPTCHA attestation (invokeWithGooglePlayIntegrity, invokeWithApnsSecret, invokeWithReCaptcha) and instead reports the demand and stops.

impl.notes: CONTROL-ONLY. tlgr drives the whole DH handshake - getDhConfig (validating the 2048-bit safe prime locally, never trusting the server), g_a_hash in phone.requestCall, then phone.confirmCall with the real g_a and key fingerprint once the callee answers - and reports the relay list a media engine would use, but it has no tgcalls binding: `media` is always "none" and the callee hears silence. --auto-discard exists so automation cannot leave a ringing call open. phoneCallProtocol is the frozen legacy constant set (min_layer=65, max_layer=92, udp_p2p, udp_reflector, library_versions). Blocked by the callee's privacyKeyPhoneCall (USER_PRIVACY_RESTRICTED); CALL_PROTOCOL_LAYER_INVALID / PARTICIPANT_VERSION_OUTDATED for old peers. Warns when an updatePhoneCall says another call is already active. A PSTN number without a Telegram account cannot be dialled at all.

flags.name: --join
flags.help: Also join it immediately - needs the E2E material below.

flags.name: --public-key
flags.help: Your int256 E2E public key (with --join).

flags.help: Pre-built e2e.chain block for subchain 0 (with --join).

flags.help: tgcalls join payload (with --join).

flags.help: Join muted (with --join).

impl.notes: Without --join this is the easiest conference operation there is: no crypto, one RPC, and you get back groupCall.invite_link - the shareable call link. With --join the API additionally wants a fresh E2E public key, a valid initial e2e.chain block for subchain 0 and a tgcalls join payload; tlgr can build none of those, so it refuses with a usage error naming exactly what is missing rather than sending a request that will fail. conference_call_size_limit (200) caps participants.

flags.name: --qr

commands.summary: Join a conference call (requires E2E material tlgr cannot generate)

flags.name: --public-key
flags.help: Your int256 E2E public key.

flags.name: --block
flags.help: The join block, built on the current tip of subchain 0.

flags.name: --params-json
flags.help: tgcalls join payload.

flags.name: --muted
flags.help: Join muted.

flags.name: --video-stopped
flags.help: Join with video off.

flags.name: --dry-run
flags.help: show what would change and stop

impl.notes: CONTROL-ONLY and, unlike `vc join`, not usable with a synthetic payload: conferences are end-to-end encrypted, so joining means fetching the tip of subchain 0, building a signed join block (ChangeSetGroupState + ChangeSetSharedKey) on top of it, and retrying the whole thing whenever the server answers CONF_WRITE_CHAIN_INVALID. Implementing the e2e.chain block builder is a project on the scale of the rest of tlgr and is out of scope for v2 - the command exists so a future bridge (or a user with an external block builder) has a place to plug in, and without --block/--public-key it exits 2 with that explanation. join_as is always inputPeerSelf for conferences.

commands.summary: Send an E2E-encrypted in-call message, or a key-verification broadcast

flags.name: --encrypted-blob
flags.help: Pre-encrypted message payload (phone.sendGroupCallEncryptedMessage).

flags.name: --broadcast-block
flags.help: Serialized e2e.chain broadcast block: groupBroadcastNonceCommit, then NonceReveal, on subchain 1.

flags.name: --dry-run
flags.help: show what would change and stop

impl.notes: CONTROL-ONLY relay. Conference chat is end-to-end encrypted, so tlgr can carry a payload but cannot produce one: it has no shared key (that comes from the chain) and no block builder. The same is true of the emoji verification, which is a commit-reveal broadcast on subchain 1 whose fingerprint is derived from the chain hash plus every participant's nonce. Both flags exist so an external E2E implementation can drive tlgr as its transport; incoming encrypted messages surface as opaque blobs in `vc watch`.

impl.notes: MEDIA INTERNALS (the contract messages_content's `message send --file` shares). Kind detection: extension+magic for images -> inputMediaUploadedPhoto unless --as file/--as auto with a >10 MB or >10000 px image (PHOTO_INVALID_DIMENSIONS -> fall back to document); everything else is inputMediaUploadedDocument plus attributes — video: DocumentAttributeVideo(duration,w,h,supports_streaming,round_message,nosound_video); audio: DocumentAttributeAudio(duration,title,performer); voice: DocumentAttributeAudio(voice=True,duration,waveform); gif: DocumentAttributeAnimated (plus nosound_video for a silent mp4 that must stay a video); sticker: DocumentAttributeSticker(alt,stickerset). Telethon fills duration/w/h only when hachoir is installed and resizes photos only when Pillow is — tlgr probes with ffprobe and passes explicit attributes, and errors clearly (not silently 1x1) when neither is available. Telethon 1.44 has NO kwarg for spoiler, invert_media (--caption-above), video_cover/video_timestamp, live_photo, stickers (--attached-sticker) or paid media: build types.InputMediaUploaded{Photo,Document}(..., spoiler=, ttl_seconds=, stickers=, video_cover=, video_timestamp=, live_photo=) and call messages.SendMediaRequest(..., invert_media=, effect=) / SendMultiMediaRequest([InputSingleMedia(media, random_id, message, entities)]) directly. Albums: each item goes through messages.uploadMedia first, then sendMultiMedia (<=10, homogeneous documents/audios, photos+videos may mix); FILE_REFERENCE_%d_EXPIRED names the failing index. Transfer: 512 KB parts, saveFilePart(+md5)/inputFile below 10 MB and saveBigFilePart/inputFileBig above; part count is capped by upload_max_fileparts_default/_premium from help.getAppConfig (~2 GB / 4 GB) so --dry-run can refuse before wasting the upload; FILE_PART_X_MISSING means re-send that one part, FILE_PART_SIZE_CHANGED means the chunker is inconsistent, FLOOD_PREMIUM_WAIT_X is a throttle to sleep through. `-` as the path streams stdin: spooled to a temp file by default, or true streamed upload with file_total_parts=-1 until the last part (never valid for photos); this is also the `send long text as a .txt` path (--name notes.txt --as file), taken automatically when a caption exceeds caption_length_limit. --no-send stops after messages.uploadMedia and prints the InputPhoto/InputDocument as a file id so the same bytes can feed several chats, sticker creation or a paid post. While uploading, the peer sees the right action (client.action(chat,'photo'|'video'|'document'|'audio'|'round') = messages.setTyping with sendMessageUpload*Action(progress), refreshed every ~4 s) unless --no-action. Sending an existing document/photo re-uses id+access_hash+file_reference and retries once after refreshing the reference from its source on FILE_REFERENCE_EXPIRED. Custom emoji in captions are MessageEntityCustomEmoji wrapping the alt emoji — accepted via --entities or <tg-emoji emoji-id=..> in --parse html (Telethon's HTML parser understands that tag; it does NOT understand <tg-spoiler>, tlgr injects MessageEntitySpoiler itself); non-free emoji need Premium (PREMIUM_ACCOUNT_REQUIRED). --quality high means 'upload the original bytes' and is the default; 'standard' needs ffmpeg/Pillow and is refused with a named error when they are missing. Secret-chat peers are rejected with a documented error: Telethon implements no MTProto 2.0 E2E layer, so encrypted media is explicitly out of scope for v2. Sending an existing sticker from an installed set is `message send --sticker <set>/<n>` (messages_content); `--as sticker` here is for uploading a fresh WebP/TGS/WebM.

args.help: Any https://t.me/… or tg://… link, or a bare slug.

flags.name: --no-network
flags.help: Classify from the URL only; perform no resolve call.

flags.name: --open
flags.help: Perform the follow-up read for the classified kind (preview an invite, fetch the message/story, check a gift code).

flags.name: --draft
flags.help: For msg_url / business links: save the carried text as a draft here.

impl.notes: One dispatcher, one discriminated union. kind ∈ {public-username, phone, invite, chatlist-invite, message, private-post, story, bot-start, bot-startgroup, bot-startchannel, webapp, business-chat-link, contact-token, proxy, boost, giftcode, unique-gift, stars-topup, wallpaper, theme, stickerset, emojiset, share-url, settings-section, contacts-section, login-code, confirm-phone, invoice, premium-offer, unknown}. Ambiguity rules: t.me/+X is a PHONE when X parses as a valid number, otherwise an invite hash — try resolvePhone then checkChatInvite. t.me/c/<id>/<msg> carries a bare channel id, so the access hash must come from the per-account peer cache — fail loudly (exit 5) instead of guessing. Unknown tg:// paths fall back to help.getDeepLinkInfo (path only, no query). Resolution NEVER acts: joining, starting a bot, installing a theme/stickerset, enabling a proxy, applying a boost or redeeming a gift are separate confirmed commands in their own domains, named in delegated_to. layer_gap: false

commands.notes: Also covers the classification-only entries: contacts-users.contacts-deeplink-sections (not-applicable as an RPC — reported as {kind: contacts-section, section: new|search|sort|invite|manage}) and contacts-users.resolve-account-maintenance-links (classified here, acted on in auth / profile / payments).

coverage_notes.note: delegated from messages_content: contact token export|import. (catalog cli.proposed)

args.name: ref
args.help: @username, id, marked id, +phone, t.me link, me.

flags.name: --from-chat
flags.help: Context chat for a `min` user/channel.

flags.help: Message id in --from-chat where the peer was seen.

flags.name: --until
flags.help: Also emit the id in the other id space.

flags.help: Never hit the network (get_input_entity only).

impl.notes: Resolution order: cache → resolveUsername/resolvePhone → getPeerDialogs → dialog-list scan → contacts.search. There is NO method that turns a bare id into an access hash, so an uncached numeric id must fail with exit 13/5 rather than guess — this is exactly the trap `user dialog-status` was built around. For a `min` peer, --from-chat/--from-message build inputPeerUserFromMessage / inputUserFromMessage / inputChannelFromMessage, which Telethon never builds itself; that is what makes `chat posters` output actionable. Access hashes are per-account: never print them, never share them between accounts. layer_gap: false

impl.telethon: raw: functions.stickers.SuggestShortNameRequest(title); CheckShortNameRequest(short_name); functions.messages.UploadMediaRequest(peer='me', media=InputMediaUploadedDocument(...)) per file; functions.stickers.CreateStickerSetRequest(user_id='me', title, short_name, stickers=[types.InputStickerSetItem(document=InputDocument, emoji='\U0001f600', keywords='smile,happy', mask_coords=types.MaskCoords(n, x, y, zoom))], masks=, emojis=, text_color=, thumb=, software=)

impl.notes: Four steps, and the order matters: suggest/check the short name, upload each file with messages.uploadMedia (bound to peer 'me') to obtain InputDocuments, then one createStickerSet carrying every InputStickerSetItem. Formats: static stickers are 512x512 WebP, animated are gzipped Lottie TGS, video are VP9 WebM, custom emoji are 100x100 — --convert resizes and re-encodes with Pillow/ffmpeg and fails with a named error (not a raw STICKER_PNG_DIMENSIONS/STICKER_VIDEO_BIG) when they are absent. --manifest is the third-party import path: a WhatsApp/Signal-style folder of images plus an emoji map becomes exactly the same createStickerSet call, which is why tg://importStickers needs no separate command. Every sticker MUST carry at least one emoji.

Privacy rules are emitted in order: base rule, then allows, then disallows (server applies the vector in order); channel stories ignore them. impl.telethon: raw only; needs a sender bound to stream_dc_id (Telethon's exported-sender API is private, so tlgr opens its own MTProtoSender for the media DC)
impl.notes: The genuinely useful headless feature: tlgr cannot play a livestream, but it can record one. Chunks are 1 MB upload.getFile requests against inputGroupCallStream(call, time_ms, scale, video_channel, video_quality) sent to groupCall.stream_dc_id, with segment_duration_ms = 1000 >> scale (clients hardcode 1000 ms). Joining first is mandatory: TIME_TOO_BIG or a flood wait means the chunk is not ready (sleep 100 ms, retry the same one), GROUPCALL_JOIN_MISSING / GROUPCALL_FORBIDDEN means rejoin, a fileCdnRedirect or any other error means resync from the live edge. Works for RTMP mode and for automatically-scaled stream mode; a live story is addressed by its story's call ref.

flags.name: --send-as
flags.help: Join as yourself or one of your channels (video chats/livestreams only).

flags.help: Also store --as as the chat's default (phone.saveDefaultGroupCallJoinAs).

flags.name: --muted
flags.help: Join muted.

flags.name: --video-stopped
flags.help: Join with video off.

flags.name: --invite-hash
flags.help: Speaker-link hash: grants can_self_unmute at join time.

flags.name: --params-json
flags.help: tgcalls join payload (DataJSON) produced by a real media engine.

flags.name: --listen-only
flags.help: Synthesize a listener payload instead of --params-json. Experimental - see notes.

flags.name: --dry-run
flags.help: show what would change and stop

impl.notes: CONTROL-ONLY, and the one place where that is not merely a limitation. phone.joinGroupCall's `params` is documented as a payload generated by the local tgcalls engine: a random non-zero audio ssrc, ICE ufrag/pwd and DTLS fingerprints. An empty or {} params is NOT sanctioned anywhere in the docs and must be expected to fail. So: --params-json is the supported path (bring your own engine, e.g. a bridge), and --listen-only builds a syntactically valid payload (fresh ssrc + generated ICE credentials + a self-signed DTLS fingerprint) purely to obtain server-side presence, because joining is a hard prerequisite for `vc download` (chunk fetches fail with GROUPCALL_JOIN_MISSING otherwise). --listen-only is marked experimental: its acceptance is not documented and must be verified against a live call before it ships; it never carries or plays audio, and tlgr says so in the output (`media: none`). The returned updateGroupCallConnection params tell you the playback mode: `mode` is webrtc, stream ({"stream":true}) or rtmp ({"stream":true,"rtmp":true}). Remember `source` - `vc leave` needs it. Errors: GROUPCALL_SSRC_DUPLICATE_MUCH, GROUPCALL_JOIN_MISSING, GROUPCALL_INVALID, INVITE_HASH_EXPIRED, GROUPCALL_PARTICIPANTS_TOO_MUCH. Live stories and conferences must be joined as inputPeerSelf.

impl.notes: No PEER means yourself (inputPeerSelf). With moderation rights a peer mute is a force-mute: the participant loses can_self_unmute. Without them the same RPC becomes 'mute for me' server-side (muted_by_you) - it is a real request, not a local toggle, so --for-me is explicit and the CLI refuses to send a moderation mute it knows will be a for-me mute unless you asked for it. impl.notes: Implements the documented version-gap algorithm: updateGroupCall / updateGroupCallParticipants carry a monotonically increasing version, must be applied in order, wait ~1s for a gap and refetch with phone.getGroupCall when the sequence breaks; `min` groupCall/groupCallParticipant constructors must never overwrite cached fields. This is the ONLY way to read in-call messages - they are not part of the chat history and no method fetches them - so a bot that logs live-story comments runs `vc watch --messages`. Conference messages arrive encrypted (updateGroupCallEncryptedMessage) and are emitted as opaque blobs, since decrypting them needs the E2E shared key tlgr cannot derive.
